title: Let no man despise thy youth (1 Timothy 4:12)
hook: be an example in word, conduct, charity, faith

segments.voice: Yesterday, spendomai: a life poured out, and a farewell that still asks for a cloak. Your line was bring my cloak and the books.

A meeting where nobody quite looks at the newest person when she speaks. A family dinner where the youngest one's opinion gets a pat on the head. In Ephesus, Timothy was that person. Paul had asked him to stay there and set some of the church's teachers straight. The letter never says how old he was, only that some might look down on him for being young. Paul's first letter to him has a line for exactly this.
screen: `THE YOUNGEST ONE IN THE ROOM.` → `TIMOTHY, LEFT AT EPHESUS.` → `A LINE FOR EXACTLY THIS.`

segments.voice: "Let no man despise thy youth: but be thou an example of the faithful in word, in conversation, in charity, in faith, in chastity." Look at what Paul doesn't say. He doesn't say demand respect. He doesn't say pull rank, or remind them who appointed you. He says: be an example. Earn it by how you live. Then he names five places to be seen. In word: how you speak. In conversation, which in the English of the Douay-Rheims means not talk but conduct, your whole way of life. In charity. In faith. In chastity, a clean heart. Then the habits that support it: attend to reading, to exhortation, to teaching. Meditate on these things, be wholly in them, so that your progress may be seen by all. Notice the last bit: progress. Paul doesn't expect Timothy to be finished. He expects him to be visibly growing. In the same spirit, Pope Francis wrote a whole letter to the young, called Christ Is Alive, insisting they are not only the future of the Church but its present. And the Church has canonized Carlo Acutis, an Italian teenager who loved computers and the Eucharist and died of leukemia at fifteen. Paul's advice cuts both ways. To the young, it says: be an example. To everyone else, it says the same thing as its first words. Don't despise them.
screen: `NOT 'DEMAND RESPECT': BE AN EXAMPLE.` · `CONVERSATION: YOUR WHOLE CONDUCT.` · `PROGRESS THAT CAN BE SEEN.` · `A SAINT WHO DIED AT FIFTEEN.` · then, large: `LET NO MAN DESPISE THY YOUTH.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone younger than you: a child, a teenager, a new coworker, a niece, a student. Think of one real thing they do well, something you've actually seen, not a general compliment, and shape it into a sentence you could say to them. If you pray, pray for them by name; if not, hold them in mind with care.
Neotes, youth. Paul to young Timothy: don't demand respect; be an example in word, conduct, charity, faith and chastity. Today's word.
Your line: be an example. Respect earned by how you live, not demanded. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Catholic Church holds World Youth Day gatherings, and Pope Francis addressed young people directly in the 2019 apostolic exhortation Christus Vivit; young saints such as Carlo Acutis are held up as examples.

chat.meaning: Let no man despise thy youth, but be an example. Paul says earn it by how you live, and let your progress be seen.

Ephesus.meaning: the city where Paul asked Timothy to stay

Christ Is Alive.meaning: Pope Francis's letter to young people

Carlo Acutis.meaning: an Italian teenager, now a saint, who died at fifteen

Douay-Rheims.meaning: the old Catholic English translation of the Bible

sources.quoted: Let no man despise thy youth: but be thou an example of the faithful in word, in conversation, in charity, in faith, in chastity.

sources.ref: Francis, Christus Vivit (2019); canonization of Carlo Acutis (2025)

notes: Timothy's age is unknown; 'young' (neotēs) in antiquity could describe adults up to about forty. Confirm phrasing.
Christus Vivit, post-synodal apostolic exhortation, March 2019; the 'not only the future but the present' theme (e.g. CV 64). Confirm.
Carlo Acutis: died October 2006 of leukemia, aged 15; canonized September 7, 2025. Confirm.
Authorship of 1 Timothy debated among scholars; not raised in the voice.
